source_spans.locator: Nature Reviews Neuroscience 11, published pp.127-128, Key Points and opening derivation: viable agents occupy a restricted repertoire of states and minimize long-run sensory improbability
Nature Reviews Neuroscience 11, published p.128, Box 1: internal-state update and action minimize an accessible upper-bound objective using sensory input and an internal generative density
Nature Reviews Neuroscience 11, published pp.134-135, value/control discussion: preferred states are specified by prior expectations and action realizes expected trajectories

institutions: The Wellcome Trust Centre for Neuroimaging, University College London

conditions: adaptive agent whose viable states occupy a restricted region and whose internal dynamics encode a probabilistic model of sensory causes
substrate: internal states coupled to sensory states and actions
task: maintain state trajectories within the agent-specific viable repertoire
temporal_scope: proximal minimization of an accessible objective linked to long-run occupancy of viable states

nodes.description: restricted set of agent states whose sustained occupancy is compatible with persistence
sensory states generated by interaction between agent and world
internal probabilistic representation of hidden causes of sensory samples
internally evaluable objective that upper-bounds sensory improbability under the agent's model
change in internal sufficient statistics that improves the conditional representation of sensory causes
action that changes which sensory states are sampled from the world
prior expectations that assign high probability to state trajectories compatible with the agent's organization

relations.description: the agent-specific viable repertoire constrains which state trajectories carry high prior probability
the accessible optimization objective depends on current sensory data and the internally encoded probability density over their causes
updating internal states tightens the encoded conditional distribution and reduces the objective without directly changing current sensory data
action changes sampled sensory data so that observations become more consistent with the agent's current predictions and preferred trajectories
reducing the proximal objective is proposed as the operational route by which the agent keeps long-run sampled states within its viable repertoire
